The articulation information in Assist.org not only shows a link to the admission requirements (aka our Major Specific Criteria webpage) but also Cal State LA graduation requirements that may be completed at the lower-division level, prior to transferring to the University. The diversity requirement is a graduation requirement, not an admission requirement. The diversity requirement may be completed prior to, or after, transferring to the University.


For the Cal State LA degree, students will be required to complete two courses (six units) certified as diversity courses, at least one focusing on issues of race and ethnicity and their intersectionality with other social categories that structure inequality in society. These courses can be completed either at the lower-division or upper-division level from among courses satisfying GE requirements.


Please view the General Education agreements on Assist.org for the lower-division courses that will meet the Diversity (d) and Race & Ethnicity (re) Requirements.

Major Specific Criteria


This articulation agreement displays lower-division course requirements specific to the major. Cal State LA lower-division course numbers range from 1000 - 2999. Students are advised to seek advisement from a counselor when planning to transfer to CSU Los Angeles and refer to the University Catalog to learn more about this major and its features. Additional admissions criteria for the major can be found on the Major Specific Criteria campus website. Please note that admissions requirements can vary by term so check back to see if there are any changes.

Bachelor of Arts Degree


The Bachelor of Arts degree in Anthropology is available for those who seek a liberal arts education or who wish to prepare for advanced study and research.


The total number of units required for the Bachelor of Arts degree in Anthropology is 120 units, of which 52-54 units are in the major. Consult with an advisor for the specific number of units required in all areas of the degree including GE and free electives.


Departmental Honors Program


The Department of Anthropology offers an honors program for students who have completed at least 12 upper division units in anthropology, who have a minimum 3.25 grade point average in all anthropology courses, and who possess a minimum 3.0 grade point average in all college work. Application to the program is made by written petition.


The program is designed to introduce superior students to intensive research experience in anthropology and related fields, as well as to more sophisticated and thorough study of anthropological theory in relevant subareas of the discipline. Honor students are permitted to depart from the normal major program in various ways to broaden and enrich their curriculum.


Honor students plan their programs in consultation with an honors adviser. Students enroll during each of their final semesters in ANTH 3960, and submit a written thesis to the departmental honors committee. Diplomas and transcripts of honors program graduates are designated: \"Graduated with Departmental Honors in Anthropology.\"
